conditions: alpha is a path in X from x0 to x1.
conclusion: The map [f]->[alpha^{-1} * f * alpha], with convention adjusted to path direction, is an isomorphism between the corresponding fundamental groups.
typical_uses: Compare fundamental groups at different basepoints in path-connected spaces.
Repair basepoint changes by inserting the connecting path and possible conjugation.
common_misuses: Identifying fundamental groups at different basepoints canonically without a chosen path.
Ignoring conjugation when changing basepoints.
bridge_lemmas: Path concatenation with alpha and alpha^{-1} is invertible on loop classes.
repair_templates: Choose an explicit path between basepoints and state the induced isomorphism.

name: Continuous maps induce homomorphisms on pi1
statement: A continuous map h:X->Y sends based loops to based loops and induces a group homomorphism h_*:pi_1(X,x0)->pi_1(Y,h(x0)).
conclusion: h_*([f])=[h o f] is a well-defined group homomorphism.
typical_uses: Use functoriality of the fundamental group in proofs.
Repair algebraic topology arguments by checking map continuity and basepoint image.
common_misuses: Applying h_* to loops based at the wrong point.
Assuming noncontinuous maps induce homomorphisms.
bridge_lemmas: Composition with h preserves path homotopies and concatenation of paths.
repair_templates: State the basepoint image h(x0) and verify h o H is a valid path homotopy.

name: Functoriality of fundamental group
statement: The identity map induces the identity homomorphism on pi_1, and composition of maps induces composition of the corresponding homomorphisms.
conditions: f:X->Y and g:Y->Z are continuous maps.
conclusion: (g o f)_*=g_* o f_* and (id_X)_*=id_{pi_1(X,x0)}.
typical_uses: Compute induced maps by factoring continuous maps.
Repair proofs involving commuting diagrams of fundamental groups.
common_misuses: Forgetting basepoints when composing induced homomorphisms.
Reversing the order of induced homomorphism composition.
bridge_lemmas: (g o f) o loop = g o (f o loop).
repair_templates: Write the basepointed maps and induced homomorphisms explicitly before composing.

name: Covering map
statement: A covering map p:E->B is a continuous surjection such that each point of B has an open neighborhood evenly covered by p.
conditions: For every b in B, there is an open U containing b such that p^{-1}(U) is a union of disjoint open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p.
conclusion: p is a covering map and E is a covering space of B.
typical_uses: Verify covering-space hypotheses before path lifting or pi_1 computations.
Repair false covering claims by checking evenly covered neighborhoods.
common_misuses: Assuming every local homeomorphism is a covering map without global evenly covered neighborhoods.
Forgetting surjectivity.
bridge_lemmas: The sheets over an evenly covered U are open and disjoint, and p restricted to each sheet is a homeomorphism onto U.
repair_templates: For each base point, exhibit a specific evenly covered neighborhood and its sheets.

name: Path lifting for covering maps
statement: A path in the base of a covering map has a unique lift once the starting point in the fiber is chosen.
conditions: e0 is in E with p(e0)=f(0).
conclusion: There exists a unique path tilde f:I->E such that tilde f(0)=e0 and p o tilde f=f.
typical_uses: Lift loops and paths to compute fundamental groups and covering transformations.
Repair covering-space proofs by specifying the starting lift point.
common_misuses: Claiming uniqueness without fixing the starting point.
Lifting paths for maps that are not known to be coverings.
bridge_lemmas: Subdivide I so the path image on each subinterval lies in an evenly covered neighborhood.
repair_templates: Choose e0 in the correct fiber, then construct the lift locally over evenly covered neighborhoods.

name: Homotopy lifting for covering maps
statement: A homotopy into the base of a covering map lifts uniquely once a lift of the initial map is fixed.
conditions: H:X x I->B is a homotopy.
tilde h_0:X->E is continuous and p o tilde h_0=H(-,0).
The standard hypotheses of the covering homotopy theorem in the text are satisfied.
conclusion: There is a unique lifted homotopy tilde H:X x I->E with p o tilde H=H and tilde H(-,0)=tilde h_0.
typical_uses: Show endpoint behavior of lifted homotopic paths and derive pi_1 information.
Repair arguments that lift homotopies without initial lift data.
common_misuses: Trying to lift a homotopy without specifying the initial lift.
Applying the theorem outside covering maps.
bridge_lemmas: Path lifting uniqueness controls the lift on vertical paths t->H(x,t).
repair_templates: Provide the initial lifted map and check the map is a covering before invoking homotopy lifting.

name: Fundamental group of the circle
statement: The fundamental group of the circle is isomorphic to the additive group of integers.
conditions: S^1 is based at a point x0.
conclusion: pi_1(S^1,x0) is isomorphic to Z, with isomorphism given by winding number.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups using maps to or from the circle.
Repair proofs of noncontractibility of S^1.
common_misuses: Assuming all loops in S^1 are null-homotopic.
Ignoring basepoint conventions in the generator.
bridge_lemmas: The covering map R->S^1, t->exp(2 pi i t), identifies loop classes with integer endpoint changes of lifts.
repair_templates: Lift the loop to R starting at a chosen lift and compute the integer endpoint difference.

name: No retraction from disk to boundary circle
statement: There is no continuous retraction from the disk D^2 onto its boundary circle S^1.
conditions: r:D^2->S^1 is assumed continuous with r restricted to S^1 equal to the identity.
conclusion: No such retraction r exists.
typical_uses: Prove fixed point and extension impossibility results.
Repair arguments that assume a disk retracts onto its boundary.
common_misuses: Defining a radial projection on the disk without handling the origin.
Forgetting the map must restrict to the identity on the boundary.
bridge_lemmas: A retraction would make the induced map pi_1(S^1)->pi_1(D^2)->pi_1(S^1) equal the identity, impossible since pi_1(D^2) is trivial.
repair_templates: Replace a claimed retraction with a map defined only on D^2\{0}, or prove no continuous extension exists.

name: Brouwer fixed point theorem for disk
statement: Every continuous map from a closed disk to itself has a fixed point.
conclusion: There exists x in D^2 such that f(x)=x.
typical_uses: Prove existence of fixed points in planar disk settings.
Repair fixed-point arguments by reducing to the no-retraction theorem.
common_misuses: Applying the theorem to noncompact or nonconvex domains without a homeomorphic disk argument.
Assuming uniqueness of the fixed point.
bridge_lemmas: A fixed-point-free map would define a retraction from the disk to its boundary by projecting from f(x) through x.
repair_templates: Show the domain is homeomorphic to a closed disk and the map is continuous before applying the theorem.

name: Deformation retract induces pi1 isomorphism
statement: If A is a deformation retract of X, then inclusion A->X is a homotopy equivalence and induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups.
conditions: A is a subspace of X.
There is a deformation retraction of X onto A.
conclusion: The inclusion-induced map pi_1(A,x0)->pi_1(X,x0) is an isomorphism.
typical_uses: Compute pi_1 by replacing a space with a deformation retract.
Repair fundamental-group computations by proving deformation retract, not just homotopy-like intuition.
common_misuses: Using a retraction that is not part of a deformation retraction to claim homotopy equivalence.
Moving the basepoint outside A.
bridge_lemmas: A deformation retraction gives maps i and r with r o i=id_A and i o r homotopic to id_X.
repair_templates: Construct the deformation homotopy explicitly or cite a standard deformation retract.

name: Homotopy equivalence preserves pi1
statement: A homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups, with basepoint paths handled when homotopies move basepoints.
conditions: Basepoint changes from the homotopies are accounted for when necessary.
conclusion: f_*:pi_1(X,x0)->pi_1(Y,f(x0)) is an isomorphism up to the standard basepoint-change adjustment.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups up to homotopy type.
Repair pi_1 arguments that rely on spaces merely being homotopy equivalent.
common_misuses: Ignoring basepoint paths when the homotopy does not fix the basepoint.
Assuming a homotopy equivalence is a homeomorphism.
bridge_lemmas: Functoriality and the induced maps of homotopic maps differ by basepoint-change conjugation.
repair_templates: Choose homotopy inverse and track the path followed by the basepoint during the homotopy.

name: Higher spheres are simply connected
statement: For n>=2, the sphere S^n has trivial fundamental group.
conditions: S^n is based at any point.
conclusion: pi_1(S^n) is the trivial group.
typical_uses: Show loops in higher-dimensional spheres are null-homotopic.
Repair computations that incorrectly import pi_1(S^1)=Z to higher spheres.
common_misuses: Claiming pi_1(S^n)=Z for all n.
Ignoring the n>=2 condition.
bridge_lemmas: A loop in S^n can be homotoped to miss a point, and S^n minus a point is homeomorphic to R^n.
repair_templates: For n>=2, move the loop off a point and contract it in the punctured-sphere chart.

name: Seifert-van Kampen theorem
statement: If X is the union of path-connected open sets U and V with path-connected intersection, then pi_1(X) is obtained from pi_1(U) and pi_1(V) by amalgamating the images of pi_1(U cap V).
conditions: U and V are open and path connected.
U cap V is path connected.
A basepoint x0 lies in U cap V.
conclusion: pi_1(X,x0) is the pushout of pi_1(U,x0) and pi_1(V,x0) over pi_1(U cap V,x0).
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups from open covers.
Repair van Kampen applications by checking openness, path connectedness, and intersection hypotheses.
common_misuses: Applying van Kampen when U cap V is disconnected.
Forgetting basepoint must lie in the intersection.
bridge_lemmas: Loops can be subdivided into pieces lying alternately in U and V.
repair_templates: Choose an open cover with path-connected intersection and put the basepoint in the intersection before applying the theorem.

name: Free product universal property
statement: The free product of groups receives homomorphisms from each factor and is universal for maps from the factors into any group.
conditions: G=* G_alpha is their free product.
conclusion: For any group H and homomorphisms phi_alpha:G_alpha->H, there is a unique homomorphism Phi:G->H extending all phi_alpha.
typical_uses: State van Kampen conclusions algebraically.
Repair group presentations arising from topological decompositions.
common_misuses: Treating a free product as a direct product.
Forgetting reduced-word normal form.
bridge_lemmas: Elements of a free product have reduced-word representatives alternating among nonidentity elements of factors.
repair_templates: Use the universal property to define homomorphisms out of a free product instead of assigning inconsistent values on words.

name: Free group universal property
statement: A free group on a set S admits arbitrary functions from S into any group uniquely extended to homomorphisms.
conditions: F(S) is the free group on S.
h:S->G is a function into a group G.
conclusion: There exists a unique homomorphism H:F(S)->G extending h.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups of graphs and wedges of circles.
Repair proofs defining homomorphisms from free groups.
common_misuses: Imposing relations in a free group without quotienting by their normal closure.
Confusing a free abelian group with a free group.
bridge_lemmas: Reduced words in generators and formal inverses represent elements of F(S).
repair_templates: If relations are required, pass from the free group to a quotient by the normal subgroup generated by those relations.

name: Fundamental group of wedge of circles
statement: The fundamental group of a wedge of n circles is the free group on n generators; for an indexed wedge, it is free on the corresponding set under the text's hypotheses.
conditions: X is a wedge of circles with common basepoint.
The wedge satisfies the topological hypotheses used in the theorem version.
conclusion: pi_1(X) is a free group generated by the circle loops.
typical_uses: Compute graph and CW-complex fundamental groups.
Repair computations that incorrectly abelianize wedge-of-circle groups.
common_misuses: Claiming the wedge of two circles has pi_1 isomorphic to Z x Z instead of a free product Z * Z.
Ignoring local hypotheses for infinite wedges.
bridge_lemmas: Apply van Kampen to unions adding one circle at a time.
repair_templates: Use free product, not direct product, when combining circles at a common point.

name: Attaching a two-cell adds a relation
statement: Attaching a 2-cell to a space along a loop quotients the fundamental group by the normal closure of the attaching loop's class.
conditions: X is obtained from a path-connected space A by attaching a 2-cell along a loop f:S^1->A.
The basepoint and path choices identify the attaching loop with an element of pi_1(A).
conclusion: pi_1(X) is pi_1(A) modulo the normal subgroup generated by the attaching loop class.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups from polygonal presentations or CW complexes.
Repair surface group computations by adding the correct relation.
common_misuses: Adding a relation without taking normal closure.
Forgetting orientation or basepoint path in the attaching word.
bridge_lemmas: Van Kampen applied to the cell neighborhood makes the boundary loop null-homotopic after attachment.
repair_templates: Write the attaching loop as a word in pi_1(A), then quotient by its normal closure.

name: Fundamental group of the torus
statement: The fundamental group of the torus is isomorphic to Z x Z with presentation <a,b | aba^{-1}b^{-1}>.
conditions: T^2 is the torus with a chosen basepoint.
conclusion: pi_1(T^2) is isomorphic to Z x Z.
typical_uses: Compute maps from or to the torus using two commuting generators.
Repair presentations that forget the commutator relation.
common_misuses: Treating pi_1(T^2) as the free group on two generators.
Using the sphere's trivial group for the torus.
bridge_lemmas: The torus is obtained from a square by identifying edges with attaching word aba^{-1}b^{-1}.
repair_templates: Start with the wedge-of-two-circles group and quotient by the commutator relation.

name: Fundamental group of projective plane
statement: The real projective plane has fundamental group of order two.
conditions: RP^2 is the real projective plane with a basepoint.
conclusion: pi_1(RP^2) is isomorphic to Z/2Z.
typical_uses: Distinguish RP^2 from S^2 and compute covering relationships.
Repair surface classification arguments using fundamental groups.
common_misuses: Claiming RP^2 is simply connected.
Confusing RP^2 with the torus or Klein bottle.
bridge_lemmas: RP^2 is obtained by attaching a 2-cell to S^1 by a degree-two map, giving relation a^2=1.
repair_templates: Use the polygon word aa and quotient the free group on one generator by a^2.

name: Classification of compact connected orientable surfaces
statement: Every compact connected orientable surface is homeomorphic to a sphere with g handles for a unique genus g.
conditions: M is a compact connected orientable surface.
conclusion: There is a unique integer g>=0 such that M is homeomorphic to the orientable surface of genus g.
typical_uses: Classify compact orientable surfaces and compare invariants.
Repair surface arguments by checking compactness, connectedness, and orientability.
common_misuses: Applying the orientable classification to nonorientable surfaces.
Ignoring boundary if the theorem version assumes no boundary.
bridge_lemmas: Cutting and pasting polygonal schemas reduce surfaces to normal forms.
repair_templates: First verify whether the surface is closed or has boundary and whether it is orientable, then apply the matching classification theorem.

name: Classification of compact connected nonorientable surfaces
statement: Every compact connected nonorientable closed surface is homeomorphic to a connected sum of k projective planes for a unique positive integer k.
conditions: M is a compact connected nonorientable closed surface.
conclusion: There is a unique k>=1 such that M is homeomorphic to the connected sum of k copies of RP^2.
typical_uses: Classify nonorientable compact surfaces.
Repair classification proofs that mix orientable and nonorientable normal forms.
common_misuses: Calling a connected sum of projective planes orientable.
Forgetting uniqueness of the nonorientable genus parameter.
bridge_lemmas: Polygonal edge identifications can be transformed into a standard product of square terms.
repair_templates: Determine orientability first, then reduce the polygonal schema to the nonorientable normal form.

name: Lifting criterion for covering spaces
statement: A map into the base of a covering lifts exactly when the induced subgroup on pi_1 is contained in the subgroup coming from the covering, under the usual path-connected and locally path-connected hypotheses.
conditions: X is path connected and locally path connected, with basepoint x0.
conclusion: There exists a lift tilde f:X->E with tilde f(x0)=e0 and p o tilde f=f.
typical_uses: Decide whether maps lift to a covering space.
Repair lifting claims by checking the induced subgroup condition.
common_misuses: Assuming every map lifts to every covering.
Ignoring the chosen point e0 in the fiber.
bridge_lemmas: Loops in X must lift to loops in E when transported through f.
repair_templates: Compute f_* on pi_1 and verify subgroup containment for the chosen lift point.

name: Universal covering space
statement: A universal covering space is a covering space whose total space is simply connected.
conditions: E is path connected and simply connected.
conclusion: p:E->B is a universal covering of B.
typical_uses: Compute all covering spaces via subgroups of pi_1.
Repair claims that a covering is universal by checking simple connectedness of the total space.
common_misuses: Calling a covering universal merely because it covers the whole base.
Forgetting path connectedness assumptions.
bridge_lemmas: Universal covers, when they exist under standard hypotheses, are unique up to covering equivalence.
repair_templates: Prove the covering total space is simply connected, often by deformation retract or known pi_1 computation.

name: Classification of covering spaces by subgroups
statement: For suitable spaces, path-connected covering spaces of B correspond to conjugacy classes of subgroups of pi_1(B).
conditions: B is path connected, locally path connected, and semilocally simply connected.
Covering spaces are considered up to equivalence over B.
conclusion: Equivalence classes of path-connected coverings correspond to conjugacy classes of subgroups of pi_1(B).
typical_uses: Classify coverings and construct covers from subgroup data.
Repair covering classification arguments by checking local hypotheses.
common_misuses: Ignoring conjugacy when basepoints are not fixed.
Applying the classification when the base is not semilocally simply connected.
bridge_lemmas: A covering p:E->B determines the subgroup p_*(pi_1(E,e0)) of pi_1(B,b0).
repair_templates: State whether coverings are based or unbased; use subgroups for based covers and conjugacy classes for unbased covers.

name: Deck transformations and normal coverings
statement: For a path-connected covering, deck transformations act on fibers; for normal coverings this action is transitive and the deck group is related to the quotient of pi_1 of the base by the covering subgroup.
conditions: p:E->B is a path-connected covering map.
The covering subgroup H=p_*(pi_1(E,e0)) is normal in pi_1(B,b0) for the normal-cover quotient statement.
conclusion: In the normal case, the deck transformation group is isomorphic to pi_1(B,b0)/H under the standard identification.
typical_uses: Compute symmetry groups of coverings and normal covers.
Repair deck-group computations by checking normality of the subgroup.
common_misuses: Assuming every covering is normal.
Identifying the deck group with the full pi_1(B) when the covering subgroup is nontrivial.
bridge_lemmas: A deck transformation is determined by the image of one point in a fiber for connected covering spaces.
repair_templates: Compute the covering subgroup and check normality before forming the quotient group.

name: Graph fundamental group by spanning tree
statement: A connected graph has fundamental group free on the edges not in a maximal tree.
conditions: G is a connected graph viewed as a topological space.
T is a maximal tree in G.
conclusion: pi_1(G) is a free group with one generator for each edge of G not in T.
typical_uses: Compute fundamental groups of graphs and one-dimensional complexes.
Repair graph pi_1 computations by choosing a maximal tree.
common_misuses: Counting all edges instead of only edges outside a maximal tree.
Using a nonmaximal or disconnected tree without adjustment.
bridge_lemmas: Collapsing a maximal tree gives a wedge of circles, one for each remaining edge.
repair_templates: Find a maximal tree, collapse it, and count the remaining independent edge loops.

name: Subgroups of free groups are free
statement: Every subgroup of a free group is free.
conditions: H is a subgroup of F.
conclusion: H is a free group.
typical_uses: Use covering spaces of graphs to prove algebraic subgroup results.
Repair group-theory arguments that assume subgroups of free groups have arbitrary relations.
common_misuses: Assuming a subgroup of a free group must have finite rank.
Confusing free group with free abelian group.
bridge_lemmas: Realize F as pi_1 of a graph and H by a covering graph; graph fundamental groups are free.
repair_templates: Construct the corresponding covering graph or cite the Nielsen-Schreier theorem.
